posts.title: A small AI support inbox loop
posts.promise: Triage one kind of ticket, draft a sourced reply, and leave approval to a person.
posts.whatItIs: Auxx describes a support CRM where an agent can read tickets, retrieve relevant customer records and knowledge, draft replies, and update records. A beginner version could handle one narrow ticket type using a small sample inbox and a written procedure, rather than rebuilding the full CRM.
posts.whoPays: Hypothesis: a small online shop or support team with repetitive questions might pay for less routine inbox work. The supplied page does not establish paying customers or demand.
loop: A new test ticket or scheduled run starts the workflow.
The system finds the relevant customer record and approved policy text.
A written procedure routes the ticket to one supported category.
The model drafts a reply using retrieved material and marks uncertain cases.
A person reviews the draft and decides whether to send it.
The workflow records the category and outcome for later review.
posts.evidence: Auxx’s first-party page describes ticket-created and scheduled triggers, procedures written in plain language, an agent that reads tickets and drafts replies, access limits, knowledge retrieval, and record updates. These are maker-described capabilities; the page does not verify customer results.
posts.uncertainty: The page presents product screens and feature claims, not independent usage results. A student prototype would need sample data, a narrow policy set and review before sending; retrieval can miss context, and people must write procedures, handle exceptions and approve sensitive replies. This loop does not establish that the whole business runs autonomously.
first24Hours: Choose one low-risk ticket category and write a five-rule response policy.
Create ten fictional tickets and matching policy snippets in a local table.
Prototype retrieval plus reply drafts, then compare every draft with a human-written expected answer.

ease.reason: A narrow ticket triage prototype can use sample tickets and written procedures; integrations add work.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small support teams may pay to reduce repetitive ticket handling; demand is unproved.

feasibility.reason: A single ticket category, grounded draft, and approval step fit a small two-week experiment; live integrations are extra scope.

autonomy.reason: The page describes ticket-created and scheduled triggers, retrieval, drafts, and record updates; humans define procedures and review sensitive replies.

evidence.reason: First-party page shows product screens and describes workflows, but no independently verified use or outcomes.

steps.message: Assessed all 12 frozen enrichment leads and their attached sources. Proposed one bounded support-ticket loop at the unrounded policy threshold; rejected the other eleven for limited evidence, scope, or no specific operating loop.
